result:
The proposed answer 1/r! is incorrect. I get r/(r+1), by treating the problem as one about the lattice of exponent vectors.

Write each S-smooth number as n = ∏ p_i^{x_i} with x ∈ ℕ^r. The forbidden set {n, p_1 n, …, p_r n} then becomes the configuration {x, x+e_1, …, x+e_r}. The numbers up to X correspond to a large simplex-shaped region. Almost all of its points lie far from the boundary, so boundary effects do not change the limiting density.

**Upper bound on the kept density.** Let R be the set of removed points. Each removed point lies in at most r+1 configurations (as x or as some x+e_i). Every configuration must contain a removed point. So R must have density at least 1/(r+1), and the kept set has density at most r/(r+1).

**Matching construction.** Remove all x with ∑ i·x_i ≡ 0 (mod r+1). For any configuration, the values of ∑ i·x_i on x, x+e_1, …, x+e_r are c, c+1, …, c+r. These are all distinct residues mod r+1, so exactly one is 0. Hence every configuration loses exactly one point, and the removed density is exactly 1/(r+1).

Therefore the limit is r/(r+1). The proposed answer 1/r! does not match this. For r = 2, for example, it gives 1/2, whereas the correct value is 2/3. The proposed solution also gives no actual derivation.

VERDICT: REJECT
